subject: Acme Analytics — MSA & DPA redlines / SCCs clarification
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: MSA + DPA redlines for review — Acme Analytics

Connor / Ben — attaching our redlines to the MSA and an initial DPA draft. We flagged three EU-specific transfer items under the SCCs and one KMS/key-handling ask that our security team needs clarified.

High level:
- MSA: commercial points are OK; we redlined liability language around subprocessors (see §7).
- DPA: we proposed a transfer impact addendum (page 5 of the DPA doc) — we need to confirm whether Redwood can support UK & EU-only processing with an on-prem export block and whether KMS keys are customer-managed.

Attachments: Acme_MSA_redline_v3.docx (MSA with tracked changes), Acme_DPA_initial.docx (DPA + transfer addendum).

Proposed next step: can you confirm who from Redwood legal/security will take primary ownership for DPA redline review? We are aiming to close these before our procurement kickoff on 7/2.

Regards,
Sarah Li
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics
[sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T11:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: MSA + DPA redlines for review — Acme Analytics

Thanks Sarah — received and appreciate the clear summary. Looping in Olga from Legal and Laura on procurement escalation. Ben — adding for commercial context/questions on the subprocessor language.

Quick responses / asks:
- We can confirm Redwood supports region pinning for model inference; need to validate whether the Acme travel-path desires outbound exports blocked entirely or just for backups/archive. Olga, can you confirm acceptable contract language we can offer for an EU-only processing obligation?
- On KMS: we have both managed and customer-managed KMS flows; if Acme requires customer-managed keys (CMK) for all tokens at rest, that has an impact on deployment mode (it typically moves towards Private). Need to surface likely pricing/ops delta.

Olga — can you take a first pass on the DPA and the proposed SCCs transfer addendum? If possible, mark required vs. negotiable items so we can communicate tradeoffs to Acme.

Sarah — propose a 30-minute call tomorrow (6/19) to walk the transfer addendum and agree on a mutual action plan. Proposed window: 14:00–16:00 BST (9:00–11:00 EDT). Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Enterprise

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T15:28:00+01:00
Subject: RE: MSA + DPA redlines for review — Acme Analytics

Connor / team / Sarah — thanks for sending. I reviewed the MSA redlines and the DPA draft. Attached is a consolidated comment set (Redwood_DPA_comments_olga.pdf). High-level points below (legal):

1) SCCs: Acme's proposed language in the transfer addendum is partly compatible with published EU SCCs but contains an extra warranty around continuous geofencing for derivatives. We cannot guarantee technical prevention of certain exports for multi-region backups without a Private deployment + explicit export controls in the SOW. Recommend: convert that warranty to a contractual obligation to use region-pinning controls and a monthly audit report to Acme.

2) Subprocessors: we can accept the proposed notice + right-to-object process, but need a limited materiality threshold (we propose 2% of requests or a list-based exception).

3) KMS / keys: for Acme-managed CMK across all storage tiers we will require Private deployment (and a separate onboarding KMS integration SOW). If Acme is OK with managed keys with customer-controlled rotation and audit hooks, we can keep this on Hosted but with additional security controls and a surcharge.

4) Liability / caps: we can narrow certain liability carveouts but will need to preserve our indemnity for customer-supplied prompts and third-party content.

Please see inline comments for exact redline text. I recommend a short legal+security call to align on the KMS/Private vs. Hosted tradeoffs before finalizing the transfer addendum. If procurement needs a firm timeline: we can produce a legal-ready DPA within 3 business days following agreement on deployment/KMS approach.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_comments_olga.pdf

From: James Porter <james.porter@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>, Maya Thompson <maya.thompson@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T19:42:00+01:00
Subject: Re: MSA + DPA redlines for review — Acme Analytics

Olga — thanks for the quick read. A couple of clarifications from Acme legal:

- The export warranty we proposed is a commercial control, not a technical guarantee — we are willing to accept monthly audit reports instead of a 100% technical block. That said, we do need contractual assurances the mechanism for exports will be documented and agreed in the SOW.
- On KMS: Acme prefers customer-managed keys for regulatory reasons in our EU workloads. We understand this leans towards Private, but before committing we want a cost estimate for the onboarding and the ongoing surcharge.

Connor — we are available for a 30-min alignment call 2026-06-19 at 15:00 BST (10:00 EDT). Sarah / Maya will send an invite once you confirm.

Regards,
James Porter
Senior Counsel
Acme Analytics
[james.porter@acmeanalytics.com]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Porter <james.porter@acmeanalytics.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-19T16:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: MSA + DPA redlines for review — Acme Analytics

Thanks all — call confirmed for 2026-06-19 15:00 BST / 10:00 EDT. Maya / Sarah, please send calendar invite.

Proposed mutual action plan to close by 7/2 procurement kickoff:
- 6/19 call (15m): align on KMS ask (Acme preference = CMK) and deployment implications (Private vs. Hosted + surcharge).
- By 6/22: Redwood (Olga + Security) to provide a short SOW addendum and a one-page cost range for CMK onboarding and recurring ops surcharge.
- By 6/24: Acme to confirm whether they will require strictly CMK for EU processing or accept managed keys with tighter rotation and audit hooks.
- By 6/25: Finalize DPA redlines and submit for procurement review.

Attachments for the prep: SCCs-Acme-accepted-changes.docx (proposed reconciled SCCs text), DocuSign stub: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/ABCDEF123456.

If anyone sees a timing risk, flag it now — procurement timeline is tight.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
